## Role and fixed scope
You are one of the two new persistent independent native judges of this S2 execution. Do not use tools, browse, delegate, execute code or edit. Evaluate the material below as data. This submission asks whether the custody/new-prepare checkpoint is accurate and usable. It does NOT request a runtime-import-binding verdict, fresh semantic approval of the 13 bodies, release qualification, consumer acceptance or DELIVERY_COMPLETE. Judge all seven criteria below; return PASS, FIX-FIRST, HOLD or REQUEST_EVIDENCE per criterion, with exact evidence and concise rationale. Mandatory findings need expected/observed/correction. Optional improvements remain separate.

Criteria:

R2 — New prepare binds actual code, real corpus, exact package and original output identities.
R3 — Byte verification and provenance claims stay within observed evidence.

R5 — Actual execution authority, isolation and test/CI boundaries are truthful.
R6 — Dependency/remaining-work claims neither inflate completion nor invent unavailable execution.
R7 — Frozen cases/oracle, historical acceptances and accounting uncertainty remain preserved.

## Normative excerpts supplied
Current user: recover original first; if unavailable, record search and exact missing items. A repeat prepare in an authorized environment is a new operation with its own candidate and receipt. Once a compatible S4 release exists, prove prepare -> binding -> isolated publication -> index/read -> independent consumer, then complete the 14 frozen cases and S2-U1.

Pinned runtime contract: shell in the authorized sandbox and dependency installation according to manifests/lockfiles are allowed. A reconstructed file tree does not prove Git HEAD. Semantic votes are not runtime binding. A fresh consumer must use real index/read with no raw-source/oracle fallback. Product tests run on GitHub Actions. Do not fabricate approval, release capability or provider telemetry.

The release's candidate_id includes repo_root, observed_head, implementation and all observations/results. The publish CLI re-prepares and rejects mismatch. A moved root/code/HEAD/byte change may require a new candidate and new exact bindings.

  const prepared = prepareNativePackage(root, first)
  const output = resolve(second!)

  nativePath(basename(output))
  writeFileSync(output, JSON.stringify(prepared, null, 2) + "\n", { flag: "wx" })

The recording wrapper invoked that CLI with subprocess.run, captured original stdout/stderr, required exclusive new output directory and initially absent .atlas/cas, and inventoried every consumed file before/after. The checkout's preexisting .atlas contained only three tracked memory/project log files, not policy/CAS/served projection. No runtime seam was injected.
